title: Restaurant Brands Asia Ltd - 543248 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: RBA India Q4 FY26 SSSG hit 6.3%, the highest in 12 quarters, while Indonesia took a INR120 crore impairment and the company is being acquired by Inspira Global.
summary.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 SSSG of 6.3%, up from 4.5% in the prior quarter, with full-year SSSG at 4%. Full-year revenue was INR2,271 crore, restaurant EBITDA margin 11.6% and company EBITDA margin 5.8%. Gross margin exited Q4 at 70.2%, ahead of the FY29 target. Indonesia drew a INR120 crore impairment on a DCF valuation, with Popeyes (24 outlets) losing IDR25 billion, and the company is set to be acquired by Inspira Global, with revised outlook promised after the deal closes in Q1.

segments.name: India (Burger King)
segments.commentary: Q4 SSSG 6.3%, FY26 SSSG 4%; net 68 stores opened in FY26, within 60-80 annual guidance. Restaurant EBITDA 11.6%, company EBITDA 5.8%. Dine-in traffic up 18% over three years; 91% of orders digital.

segments.name: Indonesia (Burger King)
segments.commentary: Store-level EBITDA positive IDR8 billion for FY26 and positive in Q4; dine-in ADS month-on-month above prior year except one September blip. Delivery ADS cut in Q4 for margin repair, now back to 6.2-6.4 range per management.

segments.name: Indonesia (Popeyes)
segments.commentary: 25 restaurants reduced to 24 after one closure; management described the business as struggling and said it should move to another owner's portfolio. FY26 loss IDR25 billion.

segments.name: Café / beverages
segments.commentary: BK Café now in all restaurants except a few with location limits. Management has not put marketing money behind Café except a 4-week window last year; long-term ADS goal of INR25,000 per restaurant per day over 4-5 years. Current new Café restaurants run below average.

guidance_outlook: Free cash flow neutral for India business targeted in 4-6 quarters (Sumit); analyst read this as FY28 FCF-positive, management confirmed the target.
Revised company outlook to be given in Q1 FY27 once the Inspira Global acquisition closes.
Annual net restaurant openings of 60-80 to continue.
Electric broiler (uses about half the utilities) to be installed in all India restaurants within about two months; solar rollout continues.
Indonesia BK restaurant-level EBITDA expected to cover its G&A about four quarters away, or in the year after the current one (Varman); no timeline given for Popeyes.
Management did not give new gross margin targets beyond 70%; will return at an appropriate time.
capex_capacity: Net 68 restaurants opened in FY26; cluster strategy used to place new suppliers near restaurants.
Electric broiler rollout across India restaurants nearing completion; one more round of installs pending.
Electric fryer portfolio being expanded for vegetarian items; LPG-to-PNG conversions under way where PNG is available.
Indonesia long-term strategy plan being prepared; funding requirement to be disclosed later, no figure given.
demand_pricing: Value anchored on 2for79 and 2for99 price points; coupon/app deals and shareable meal bundles also drive dine-in traffic.
Premium layer (King's Collection, Whopper Deluxe range, Korean LTO, Kimchi ad) lifting APC; management did not share Deluxe product mix or SSSG contribution.
Gross margin gains credited to cluster-led supply chain, delivery product-mix and discount changes, and high-margin add-ons (fizz drinks, Waffle Cone).
Delivery profitability improved by 2% by lowering discounts and changing product mix; management did not quantify the margin improvement further.
Management said there is no current danger to India operations from the LNG/LPG supply disruption; no restaurants closed for a day, but LPG-dependent outlets faced challenges.

qa_highlights.question: How has Café ADS performed in mature stores, and what is the incremental ADS?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not disclose Café split. Early-converted cohorts sit well above average. Target is around INR25,000 per restaurant per day over 4-5 years. Newer Café stores have lower volumes.

qa_highlights.question: Explain the cash burn (about INR350 crore used in operations, cash down from about INR500 crore to about INR150 crore) and the outlook.
qa_highlights.answer: Sumit said cash is about INR190 crore as of March, cash from operations rose from INR99 crore to INR132 crore, and India is targeting FCF neutrality in 4-6 quarters. Q4 generated INR40 crore. Analyst confirmed FY28 FCF-positive target; management agreed.

qa_highlights.question: Why was INR120 crore impairment booked, is this a full exit, what is the new promoter's plan, and what is the Indonesia breakeven timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Impairment came from a DCF on consolidated Indonesia business; management called it a one-time provision fully covering the balance-sheet requirement. Varman declined to give a timeline or exit decision until the new promoter aligns. Sumit said the BK side needs about four more quarters to cover its own G&A.

qa_highlights.question: Will Lenexis (promoter's Chinese wok brand) be merged or licensed with RBA, and what protects minority shareholders?
qa_highlights.answer: Varman said the businesses are separate, no discussions have taken place, and the focus is on Indonesia structural changes. Deal awaits government approvals with no timing given.

qa_highlights.question: Is CCI approval the only pending item for the open offer, and how is LNG supply disruption being handled?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed that CCI approval is pending. On LNG, the new broiler is electric, about half the utilities; electric fryers are being added; LPG restaurants converted to PNG where possible. No percentage split given.

qa_highlights.question: How much of gross margin expansion comes from product mix versus sourcing?
qa_highlights.answer: Varman said it is a combined effort: cluster-based supplier proximity lowers transport and input cost, and premium items and add-ons (fizz drinks, Waffle Cone) carry high margins. No split quantified.

risks_watch: Indonesia: INR120 crore impairment; further funding need and further write-downs not quantified; Popeyes (24 outlets) has no disposal timeline.
Pending CCI approval and government approvals for the Inspira Global / new promoter deal; revised guidance deferred until Q1 FY27.
Related-party exposure: the new promoter also runs Lenexis Foodworks (Chinese wok brand); management said no merger or licensing discussions are under way.
Cash: balance fell to about INR190 crore at March; FCF-neutral target depends on sustaining the 60-80 store opening pace.
LNG/LPG supply constraints; management shares no split between LPG and electric or induction cooking.
summary.management_tone: Confident on India (SSSG, margins, trend into early FY27) and guarded on Indonesia and Popeyes, where management repeatedly declined timelines and figures pending the new promoter's alignment. Evasive on Café ADS, product mix, LNG cooking split and Lenexis-related questions, citing competitive reasons or deal status.
key_quotes: we ended the fourth quarter with a 6.3% SSSG growth, which is the highest that we have achieved in the last 12 quarters, and that momentum continues.
We're working towards getting to free cash flow neutral over the next 6 to 8 quarters.
So a strong business in India and stay tuned on Indonesia.

growth.why: Management guides to 60-80 net restaurant openings a year and a free cash flow neutral India business in 4-6 quarters, with Q4 SSSG at 6.3% and FY26 SSSG at 4%; openings are backed by the cluster supply strategy, but no revenue growth figure or order book is given and the company's revised outlook awaits the Inspira deal close.
